description:
## Finding (Section C — Untrusted Input at Protocol Boundaries)

In `crate-jmap-metadata-server/src/metadata.rs`:

- Line 403 (`handle_metadata_set` update loop): `let id = Id::from(id_str.as_str());`
- Line 482 (`handle_metadata_set` destroy loop): `let id = Id::from(id_str.as_str());`

Both call sites consume `id_str` directly from the wire request (the `update` map key and the `destroy` array element, respectively) and convert it via the infallible `Id::from`, NOT the validating `Id::new_validated`.

## What goes wrong if this stays as-is?

RFC 8620 §1.2 mandates that `Id` values be SAFE-CHAR (0x21, 0x23-0x7E — visible ASCII, no `"`, no control chars, no space) and at most 255 bytes. `Id::new_validated` (jmap-types/src/id.rs:219) enforces this. `Id::from` does not.

Consequences of accepting unvalidated Ids:

1. **Spec non-conformance.** A client sending `update: {"id with space": {...}}` or `destroy: ["id\nwith\ncontrol"]` gets the same wire path as a valid Id — these should be rejected with `invalidArguments`.

2. **Per-Id length amplification within HTTP body cap.** `parse.rs:28-53` documents that the JMAP foundation expects the HTTP-transport layer (axum / hyper / etc.) to enforce body-size limits. Inside that body budget, an attacker can pack many 200-byte-Ids into a single `/set`; each one allocates a `String` on read and is cloned again into HashMap keys, error responses, and change-log entries. Validating at the boundary lets the handler reject the request before the allocation cascade.

3. **Multi-tenant log/metric pollution.** Future consumer code that includes `id.as_ref()` in log lines (e.g. metric labels, structured-log fields) cannot rely on the value being a sane string — a `\n` or `\r` in a leaked Id can corrupt log frames or label dimensions.

None of these are P0/P1 in isolation: HTTP-body-cap is the structural defense and the consumer is expected to enforce it. This finding is P2 defense-in-depth: per-Id validation closes spec-non-conformance and amplification-within-body-budget.

## Workspace cookie-cut scope (canonical-first)

The same pattern appears across every extension-server sibling — verified via `rg "Id::from\(.*str.*\)" crate-jmap-mail-server/src/`:

```
crate-jmap-mail-server/src/sieve.rs:    let id = Id::from(id_str);
crate-jmap-mail-server/src/sieve.rs:    let id = Id::from(id_str.as_str());
crate-jmap-mail-server/src/mailbox.rs:    let id = Id::from(id_str.as_str());
crate-jmap-mail-server/src/mailbox.rs:    let id = Id::from(id_str.as_str());
crate-jmap-mail-server/src/mailbox.rs:    let id = Id::from(id_str.as_str());
crate-jmap-mail-server/src/mailbox.rs:    let id = Id::from(id_str);
```

Per the workspace AGENTS.md "Canonical Templates" rule, the fix lands in `jmap-mail-server` first (it is the canonical extension-server template), then propagates to every sibling (`jmap-chat-server`, `jmap-metadata-server`, `jmap-calendars-server`, `jmap-tasks-server`, `jmap-contacts-server`, `jmap-filenode-server`, `jmap-sharing-server`).

Ideal fix shape: at each wire boundary use `Id::new_validated(id_str).map_err(|e| /* per-entry SetError invalidProperties or top-level invalidArguments */)` instead of `Id::from`. The per-entry path should produce a SetError that goes into `notUpdated` / `notDestroyed` (not a top-level error), matching the per-entry-failure RFC 8620 §5.3 atomicity rule.

## Notes

- The `extract_account_id` helper (jmap-server/src/helpers.rs:104) DOES use `Id::new_validated` for `accountId` — see its test at helpers.rs:365. The gap is per-entry Ids in `update` map keys and `destroy` array elements.
- The `filter_changes_array` `Id::from` at metadata.rs:236 is NOT in scope of this finding — those Ids come from the backend's `get_metadata_changes` return value, not the wire request.
- This finding does not block the metadata-server epic; it requires a workspace-wide sweep epic.
title: Section C: Id values from /set update keys and destroy array bypass Id::new_validated boundary check (workspace cookie-cut)
